summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, tone, or output format consistently, or teach it a narrow domain/task that prompting and few-shot examples cannot reliably achieve. RAG is better when the goal is to inject fresh or proprietary factual knowledge that changes frequently, while prompt engineering is the cheapest first step for most use cases. In practice, teams exhaust prompting and RAG first, then fine-tune to lock in style, reduce token/latency costs, and improve reliability on repetitive, well-defined tasks.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, tone, or formatting that prompting cannot reliably enforce at scale.
Fine-tune when you have a large set of high-quality labeled examples for a narrow, repetitive task (classification, extraction, domain-specific generation).
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the underlying knowledge changes frequently or must cite up-to-date, verifiable sources.
Fine-tune to cut inference costs and latency by replacing long few-shot prompts with a smaller, specialized model.
